title: Local description and size of a generated sheaf dg submodule
statement:
Fix the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $X$ be a topological space, $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings, $\mathcal A$ a sheaf dg $\mathcal O$-algebra and $M$ a left sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-module, as in [def-sfb-sheaf-dg-module-localization]. For a graded sheaf $E$ put $\|E\|=|\coprod_{U\in\operatorname{Op}(X),q\in\mathbf Z} E^q(U)|$. A dg subsheaf of $M$ means a sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-submodule: a family of $\mathcal O$-submodule sheaves $N^q\subseteq M^q$, $q\in\mathbf Z$, with $d(N^q)\subseteq N^{q+1}$ and $\mathcal A^p(V)N^q(V)\subseteq N^{p+q}(V)$ for all opens $V$ and all $p,q$. Let $F\subseteq M$ be a dg subsheaf, and let $(U_k,q_k,x_k)_{k\in K}$ be a set-indexed family with $x_k\in M^{q_k}(U_k)$. There is a smallest dg subsheaf $G\subseteq M$ containing $F$ and these sections. A section $z\in M^q(U)$ belongs to $G^q(U)$ if and only if there is an open cover $U=\bigcup_i V_i$ such that each restriction $z|_{V_i}$ is a finite sum
$$y_i+\sum_{t\in T_i}\bigl(a_{it}x_{k_t}|_{V_i}+b_{it}(d x_{k_t})|_{V_i}\bigr),$$
where $y_i\in F^q(V_i)$, $V_i\subseteq U_{k_t}$, $a_{it}\in\mathcal A^{q-q_{k_t}}(V_i)$ and $b_{it}\in\mathcal A^{q-q_{k_t}-1}(V_i)$. If $\lambda\geq\max(\aleph_0,|\operatorname{Op}(X)|,\|\mathcal A\|)$ is an infinite cardinal and $\mu\geq\lambda$ satisfies $\mu^\lambda=\mu$, then $\|F\|\leq\mu$ and $|K|\leq\mu$ imply $\|G\|\leq\mu$. All cardinals, indexing sets and sections are in the fixed universe.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, generated-submodule paragraph. Topological open-site version; replace the asserted arbitrary-cardinal maximum bound by the stated exponentiation-closed bound.

proof.text: Dg subsheaves are sheaf dg $\mathcal A$-submodules, as defined in the statement and in the source. For each open $V$ and integer $q$, let $P^q(V)\subseteq M^q(V)$ be the set of finite expressions displayed in the statement, with $y\in F^q(V)$ and every generator used defined on $V$. The empty sum gives $F^q(V)\subseteq P^q(V)$; taking $y=0$, $a=1$, $b=0$ gives $x_k\in P^{q_k}(U_k)$. Restriction restricts every coefficient and $y$. Concatenating lists, negating coefficients and multiplying coefficients by a homogeneous section of $\mathcal A$ show that $P$ is a graded submodule presheaf.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, generated-submodule paragraph; details of its local-expression construction on the open site.

proof.text: For a term with $x=x_k$ of degree $r$, the left Leibniz rule gives $d(ax+b\,dx)=(da)x+\bigl((-1)^{q-r}a+db\bigr)dx$ in degree $q+1$, since $d^2x=0$. The new coefficients have degrees $q+1-r$ and $q-r$. Also $dy\in F^{q+1}(V)$. Thus $d(P^q(V))\subseteq P^{q+1}(V)$, without adjoining any further differential generators.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, generated-submodule paragraph; details of its local-expression construction on the open site.

proof.text: Define $H^q(U)$ to consist of those $z\in M^q(U)$ whose restrictions belong to $P^q$ on an open cover of $U$. This condition is preserved by restriction, by intersecting a witness cover with the smaller open. It is local: if it holds on each member $U_j$ of a cover, the union of their witness covers is a witness cover of $U$. For two such sections use pairwise intersections of their witness covers; then the submodule property of $P$ proves closure under addition. Negation, homogeneous scalar multiplication and $d$ are checked on one witness cover using steps 1 and 2.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, generated-submodule paragraph; details of its local-expression construction on the open site.

proof.text: A compatible family in $H^q(U_j)$ glues uniquely in the sheaf $M^q$ to a section $z\in M^q(U)$. The restriction of $z$ to each $U_j$ satisfies the defining local condition, so its locality from step 3 puts $z$ in $H^q(U)$. This also works for the empty cover of the empty open. Consequently $H$ is a dg submodule sheaf. If $N\subseteq M$ is any dg submodule sheaf containing $F$ and all $x_k$, its closure under $d$ and the action puts $P^q(V)$ in $N^q(V)$. A section locally in $P$ is then locally in $N$; glue its local lifts in $N$ and use uniqueness in $M$ to see it lies in $N$. Thus $H\subseteq N$, and $G=H$ is the required smallest subsheaf and has exactly the stated local description.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), proof, generated-submodule paragraph; details of its local-expression construction on the open site.

proof.text: Assume the size hypotheses. Form an alphabet $B$ as the disjoint union of $\operatorname{Op}(X)$, $\mathbf Z$, $K$, all sections of $F$ with their open and degree labels, all sections of $\mathcal A$ with those labels, and finitely many punctuation symbols. Each summand has size at most $\mu$. A finite tagged union of sets of size at most $\mu$ embeds in $\mu\times\mu$, so $|B|\leq\mu$ by the infinite-cardinal-square lemma. A raw expression is encoded by the finite word recording its open, degree, $y$, and the ordered list of triples $(k,a,b)$. Hence the set $E$ of well-typed raw expressions has $|E|\leq|\operatorname{List}(B)|\leq\mu$ by the finite-list lemma. Evaluation yields every element of $P$; no uniqueness of expression is required.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), generated-submodule size assertion; finite-expression coding made explicit using the cited cardinal arithmetic.

proof.text: Fix $U,q$. For every $z\in G^q(U)$ choose a witness cover and expressions for its restrictions. Discard repeated opens, retaining one expression for each distinct open in the cover; its union is still $U$. Encode this witness by a function $c_z:\operatorname{Op}(X)\to E\sqcup\{*\}$, assigning the chosen expression on used opens and the extra symbol elsewhere. If two sections have the same code, they agree on the used cover and hence are equal by the sheaf uniqueness axiom. Thus this choice gives an injection of $G^q(U)$ into the function set. By the square lemma, $|E\sqcup\{*\}|\leq\mu$. Fix an injection $\operatorname{Op}(X)\hookrightarrow\lambda$ and extend codes by a fixed value outside its image; this embeds the function set into a set of size $\mu^\lambda=\mu$. Finally choose these injections for all $(U,q)$. There are at most $\mu$ such pairs, since $|\operatorname{Op}(X)|\leq\lambda\leq\mu$, $|\mathbf Z|=\aleph_0\leq\mu$, and $\mu^2=\mu$. The total section set embeds in $\mu\times\mu$, again of size $\mu$, proving $\|G\|\leq\mu$.

source.place: Tag 0FST (lemma-small-acyclics), generated-submodule paragraph, corrected topological-site size estimate: code arbitrary local gluing data using the hypothesis mu^lambda=mu.
